# Data-volume config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/data-volumes/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.DataVolumeBlock` declaring a named data volume (empty, persistent, template, or git-backed) with quota and lifecycle policy. The block label is the volume name.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `config/data-volumes` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `inventory` — the block label is the identity; the file is a container and its stem carries no meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `data_volume` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/data-volumes/<name>.hcl` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/config.DataVolumeBlock` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/config/data-volumes/reference` |

## Example

A minimal `data-volumes`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/data-volumes/example-data-volume.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

data_volume "example-data-volume" {
  lifecycle = "ephemeral"
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | — |
| `template` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `lifecycle` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `description` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `status` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `size_limit` | string | no | — | — | — | Ceiling on the volume's on-disk size, as a unit-suffixed string. Units are powers of 1024 whichever family you spell them in: "10GB", "10G" and "10GiB" all mean 10*1024^3 bytes, and B/KB/MB/GB/TB with their IEC spellings KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB are the whole vocabulary. A bare number is bytes. Anything else is refused by tera validate rather than read as zero, because zero is how the volume manager spells no ceiling at all — an operator who asked for a bound must not silently get none. Unset means no ceiling. |
